text:
riley: throwing an idea out: build a tiny web UI 'quickship' that mirrors deploy-bot CLI but focuses on safe defaults + one-click release-note generation. reduces the mental overhead for non-owners during ops windows.

cleo: sounds nice. what does "safe defaults" mean here?

riley: default canary splits (5/25/100), auto-populated change-window based on on-call calendar, and a required 'migration notes' field that blocks submission if empty. also integrates pin templating so team leads can review pins before execution.

morgan: could it also show historical ramp durations for the service so you can pick a preset (fast/normal/conservative)? we keep asking oncall for that data.

riley: exactly — quickship would fetch the last 5 rollouts and show median ramp and failure rates. UI presets map to percent/time suggestions.

ops-sre: must enforce RBAC. non-owners should be able to generate drafts and PRs but only owners/approvers can push to prod. the UI should have an "issue approver" flow that ties into release-gate.

pat: +1. Also add an escape-hatch template for immediate rollbacks that auto-populates the status-channel blurb and suggested grafana queries. makes post-rollback comms trivial.

eva: small nit: timezone handling is annoying. quickship should display change-window in local tz and UTC, and when scheduling it'll normalize to UTC in the command it generates.

riley: agreed. sample UX flow:
1) select service and target env
2) quickship fetches last rollouts and suggests presets
3) user edits release-note form (template provided)
4) click "Generate" -> shows the deploy-bot CLI equivalent, brief summary, and "Open PR" button
5) optional: click "Run dry-run" -> runs deploy-bot --dry-run and shows validation results
6) if approver, click "Execute" -> release-gate check -> deploy-bot call emitted + audit entry created

cleo: can the UI also detect overlapping change-windows? we've had two teams book the same high-risk window before.

ops-sre: yes query scheduled-rollouts DB and calendar, warn on overlap by service, and show collisions at team-level. also offer an auto-shift suggestion (e.g., recommend next free 2-hour slot).

deploy-bot: dry-run validation: conflicts found with service "auth" for 2026-05-12 14:00-16:00 UTC (simulated)

sample output riley pasted: 
```
# generated cli -> copy/paste into ops flow
/deploy-bot deploy --service payments --env prod --version v2026-05-12-rc1 \
  --pin=sha:abcd1234 --change-window="2026-05-12T14:00Z/2026-05-12T16:00Z" --canary=5,25,100 --dry-run
--- release-note ---
Service: payments
Why: db index change to reduce read tail latency
Migration: none
Monitor: payments.p99_latency, payments.errors
Rollback: /deploy-bot rollback --service payments --to=v2026-05-10
--- end ---
```

morgan: what about PR automation? we should be able to press "Open PR" and have quickship create a draft release-note PR in the right repo with labels and an autofill checklist (perf, smoke, migration).

riley: yep opt-in flow: uses a service token and creates a draft PR with the filled template and links to canary dashboards. PR body includes a short checklist that the UI can auto-check for the creator (but approver must uncheck to indicate manual verification if needed).

pat: error handling for pin mismatches is important. if the cluster returns a conflict, UI should highlight the offending flag and offer a one-click 'suggested pin' based on latest stable. forcing a pin should create a required approver step.

cleo: anything for release notes localization? support for brief vs full formats? execs like one-liner for status channels.

riley: yes two outputs: full (detailed note) and brief (single-line plus links). brief suitable for Slack post. quickship will include a "Post to Slack" button that posts the brief to the selected channel and tags the oncall.

ops-sre: retention/audit: all generated commands and PRs must be recorded to our release-audit store (we already have one). also tag with who generated vs who executed.

deploy-bot: notice: UI generated command preview will always include `--dry-run`. execution requires release-gate approval.

morgan: implementation idea: start with a static single-page app + a tiny backend service that proxies to release-gate, scheduled-rollouts DB, and GH. that keeps risk surface small.

riley: timeline proposal: week1 prototype (form + generate preview + dry-run), week2 add PR creation + audit, week3 add approvals and full execute flow.

pat: testing: make a canary in staging and exercise the full flow end-to-end during next release window. leave an invite-only beta for a couple of teams.

cleo: ok can someone spin up a quick RFC in eng-releases? include screenshots/flows and list of endpoints needed.

riley: I'll draft a short RFC and post it here by EOD. will include a demo link and a tiny checklist for privacy/permissions.

morgan: :thumbsup: excited for this, could shave 10-15min off each release for the oncall team.

riley: thanks everyone. will post RFC + prototype link shortly.

pat: tiny add: include a command export format for runbooks so SREs can embed the generated rollback snippet into incident playbooks.

riley: good call, will add export -> "runbook snippet" option.

cleo: love it. see you on the RFC."
